answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every identity post a refundable onyx bond before it can earn: the bond sits in a shared pool and is slashed if peers prove fake work. Newcomers start on a sable trial — small tasks, slow payouts — and only graduate after a trail of attested completions. Climbing to the summit of trusted, high-value work takes real time and real stake, so spinning up a hundred sock puppets costs a hundred bonds and a hundred slow climbs, while one honest agent keeps its record and its stake.
